report_name: Russian Hackers Use Zero-Click Zimbra Exploit in Global Spy Campaign

threat_actors.name: Void Blizzard
threat_actors.description: A Russian-backed cyberespionage group exploiting a zero-click vulnerability (CVE-2025-66376) in the Zimbra Collaboration Suite to steal credentials, emails, and other sensitive data from targeted organizations globally.
threat_actors.goals: Intelligence gathering for strategic, political, or economic advantage.

attack_patterns.name: Spearphishing Attachment
attack_patterns.description: The threat actor sent phishing emails containing malicious HTML as an attachment or embedded content to exploit CVE-2025-66376 in the Zimbra webmail client.

attack_patterns.name: Obfuscated Files or Information
attack_patterns.description: The malicious JavaScript payload was Base64-encoded within a `<div>` section of the HTML content to evade static analysis.

attack_patterns.name: JavaScript
attack_patterns.description: An invisible SVG element's `onload` event was used to trigger the decoding and execution of a malicious Base64-encoded JavaScript payload within the victim's browser.

attack_patterns.name: Exploit Public-Facing Application
attack_patterns.description: The campaign exploited the zero-click vulnerability CVE-2025-66376 in the public-facing Zimbra Collaboration Suite webmail platform to achieve remote code execution.

attack_patterns.name: Email Collection
attack_patterns.description: The malicious JavaScript payload exfiltrated email archives and contact lists from the victim's compromised mailbox.

attack_patterns.name: Steal Web Session Cookie
attack_patterns.description: The malicious JavaScript executed within the context of the user's authenticated webmail session to steal login credentials and other sensitive data.

attack_patterns.name: Exfiltration Over C2 Channel
attack_patterns.description: The malicious JavaScript payload sent stolen credentials, email archives, and other data to a hardcoded command and control server.

malware.name: Malicious JavaScript Payload
malware.description: A malicious JavaScript payload, obfuscated with Base64 and loaded via an SVG element, used to exploit CVE-2025-66376 in Zimbra. It exfiltrates login credentials, emails, and other data from the victim's webmail session.

vulnerabilities.name: CVE-2025-66376
vulnerabilities.description: A zero-click remote code execution vulnerability in the Zimbra Collaboration Suite (ZCS) webmail platform, exploited via specially crafted phishing emails to inject a malicious JavaScript payload without user interaction.

campaigns.name: CL-STA-1114
campaigns.description: A global cyberespionage campaign attributed to Void Blizzard, active since at least 2024, leveraging CVE-2025-66376 to compromise Zimbra webmail servers for intelligence gathering.

identities.name: Zimbra Collaboration Suite Users
identities.description: Users of the Zimbra Collaboration Suite webmail platform targeted by Void Blizzard's global espionage campaign.

infrastructure.name: Void Blizzard C2 Server
infrastructure.description: Actor-controlled command-and-control servers used to receive exfiltrated data from compromised Zimbra webmail sessions. The infrastructure is rotated periodically.

indicators.name: Zimbra Zero-Click Exploit SVG Onload
indicators.pattern:
title: Zimbra Zero-Click Exploit SVG Onload
id: 2b1a9c8d-4e5f-4a01-b8c9-d0e1f2a3b4c5
status: experimental
description: Detects emails containing an SVG element with an 'onload' attribute, a technique used by Void Blizzard to trigger a zero-click exploit (CVE-2025-66376) against Zimbra webmail clients.
references:
  - https://unit42.paloaltonetworks.com/russian-webmail-espionage/
author: cyber.netsecops.io
date: 2026-07-24
tags:
  - attack.t1566.001
  - attack.t1059.007
  - attack.initial_access
level: high
logsource:
  category: file
  product: email
detection:
  selection:
    Contents|contains|all:
      - '<svg'
      - 'onload='
  condition: selection
indicators.description: Detects emails containing an SVG element with an 'onload' attribute, a technique used by Void Blizzard to trigger the zero-click exploit CVE-2025-66376 against Zimbra.
